bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to taxation; income; providing a refundable credit for certain higher education institutions that receive certain federal funding; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 290.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[290.0696] CREDIT FOR RECEIPT OF NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH FUNDING.

Subdivision 1.

Credit allowed.

An eligible institution is allowed a credit against the tax imposed under this chapter equal to 25 percent of the amount of grants received from the National Institutes of Health in the taxable year. For purposes of this section, "eligible institution" means a public postsecondary educational institution as defined in section 136A.1465, subdivision 1, clause (4).

Subd. 2.

Credit refundable.

If the amount of credit that the taxpayer is eligible to receive under this section exceeds the liability for tax under this chapter, the commissioner shall refund the excess to the taxpayer.

Subd. 3.

Appropriation.

An amount sufficient to pay the refunds authorized under this section is appropriated to the commissioner from the general fund.

Subd. 4.

Manner of claiming.

The commissioner shall prescribe the manner in which the credit may be issued or claimed. This may include allowing the credit only as a separately processed claim for refund.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.
additions: [290.0696] CREDIT FOR RECEIPT OF NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH FUNDING.

An eligible institution is allowed a credit against the tax imposed under this chapter equal to 25 percent of the amount of grants received from the National Institutes of Health in the taxable year. For purposes of this section, "eligible institution" means a public postsecondary educational institution as defined in section 136A.1465, subdivision 1, clause (4).
If the amount of credit that the taxpayer is eligible to receive under this section exceeds the liability for tax under this chapter, the commissioner shall refund the excess to the taxpayer.
An amount sufficient to pay the refunds authorized under this section is appropriated to the commissioner from the general fund.
The commissioner shall prescribe the manner in which the credit may be issued or claimed. This may include allowing the credit only as a separately processed claim for refund.
This section is effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.
